A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T2MIR research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses and expert-routing visualizations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds loss and routing ablations, OOD evaluations, additional benchmarks and quantitative gradient-conflict analysis.

M1.justification: The token-wise and task-wise MoE architecture, balancing and contrastive objectives, momentum router, and AD/DPT training and inference procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 are retained; the new heuristic-routing and loss-removal variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: v2 adds Ant-Dir and Meta-World ML10, including generalization across distinct manipulation tasks. Appendix H also adds Cheetah-Vel tasks outside the training velocity range and testing with random-policy offline prompts. These substantially extend the original benchmark and test-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The external baselines AD, DPT, DICP, IDT and UNICORN are retained. Tables 12–13 introduce internal comparison variants that remove auxiliary losses or use fixed one-expert-per-modality routing. The added benchmark comparisons reuse the existing external baseline set.

E3.justification: Added protocols include testing velocities from U[3.1, 3.3] after training on U[0.075, 3], supplying one random-policy trajectory as an offline prompt, and ML10's split across training and evaluation task types. Appendix K additionally measures the fraction of task pairs with gradient cosine similarity below −0.05. Existing experiments retain their reported settings.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's module-removal, dataset-quality and hyperparameter studies, v2 separately ablates balancing and InfoNCE losses, compares learned routing with heuristic modality routing, tests OOD tasks and prompts, and quantifies gradient conflicts across five environments. These add substantial evidence about mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions state five random seeds and 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals for return curves. No changed run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are reported; additional return tables follow the existing reporting convention.

E6.justification: Original results are retained, while Tables 12–17 add substantial results. For example, Ant-Dir returns are 708.6±24.5 for T2MIR-DPT and 690.3±20.4 for DICP; Cheetah-Vel gradient-conflict rates are 1.2% for T2MIR-AD and 33.9% for AD. Table 15 prints DPT's Cheetah-Vel return as positive 63.2±4.4 versus −35.0±2.9 for T2MIR-DPT, contradicting the accompanying superiority claim.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, losses, mutual-information bound, Lemma 1, Theorem 1 and Appendix C proof are unchanged. Equation-reference formatting changes do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing MoE to ICRL, combining token-wise and task-wise specialization with contrastive routing, and improving AD/DPT performance. The added experiments do not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation that learned routing can better process information integrated by attention, interprets the loss ablations as showing greater sensitivity to removing balancing loss, and extends applicability claims to OOD tasks and prompts. The existing limitations concerning dataset scale, many-task contrastive learning and computational costs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents equal activated-parameter counts in the original module ablations and holding one MoE's configuration fixed while varying the other. It also supplies Ant-Dir and ML10 environment-construction details. These disclosures do not establish reruns; existing hyperparameter tables, hardware, training-time statements and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage expands to Meta-DT, LLIRL, Scalable In-context Q-learning and additional reasoning research, while bibliography entries including Decision Transformer, Prompting Decision Transformer and some theoretical ICRL work are removed. The positioning as an architectural complement to algorithmic ICRL research remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and explanation edits, updates author/contact and conference information, adds acknowledgements, and introduces appendix subsections for the additional studies. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The results presentation is substantially reorganized: v1 appendix Tables 10–11 become main-text Tables 2–3, and appendix Figure 8 becomes main-text Figure 7. v2 adds Tables 12–17 and reflows the experimental pages. Figure 2 gains descriptive panel labels; the existing plotted results are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support by isolating auxiliary-loss and routing effects, extending generalization tests, and quantifying gradient conflicts beyond v1's visualization. However, Table 15's positive DPT return contradicts its OOD-prompt superiority claim, leaving that result unresolved. The added evidence and clearer controls provide a net improvement, while the acknowledged large-scale-validation limitation remains.
